about.title: Personal Injury Help in Compton, California
about.longDescription: Compton sits at a crossroads of working-class Los Angeles County, and its streets carry heavy traffic every day. Compton Boulevard, Rosecrans Avenue, Alondra Boulevard, and Wilmington Avenue appear most often in public collision records, and the 2025 figures tell a plain story: 333 injury collisions, 484 people injured, and 3 lives lost in a city of roughly 98,000 residents. Reports also tend to bunch up on Friday afternoons between 4 and 6 p.m., when the work week winds down and the roads fill. If one of those collisions involved you, the days that followed probably brought pain, paperwork, and a stack of unanswered calls from insurers. That is where LawProactive fits in. We are a free service, not a law firm. We do not represent clients and we do not give legal advice. What we do is listen to what happened and connect you with an independent personal injury attorney who handles cases in Compton and across Los Angeles County. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery. Whether you were hurt behind the wheel, on a bicycle, walking near a bus stop, or on someone else's property, you can begin with a conversation that costs nothing and obligates you to nothing.

whyChoose.title: What California Law Means for Your Compton Claim

items.title: Two years to act, sometimes less
items.desc: Most California injury claims must be filed within two years of the incident. If a city, county, or state agency is involved, the window can shrink to six months, so timing matters.

items.title: Partial fault does not end your case
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault. Even if you share some blame for what happened, your recovery is reduced by your percentage, not wiped out.

items.title: No fixed ceiling on pain and suffering
items.desc: In an ordinary injury case, California does not cap non-economic damages such as pain, emotional distress, and loss of enjoyment of life.

items.title: Nothing out of pocket to get started
items.desc: Attorneys in the LawProactive network take cases on contingency. You owe no attorney fee unless there is a recovery in your case.

items.question: Is LawProactive a law firm?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people with an independent personal injury attorney. We do not represent you, and any attorney-client relationship is formed directly with the attorney you choose to work with.

items.question: Where do collisions in Compton tend to happen?
items.answer: Public collision records show the highest counts along Compton Boulevard, Rosecrans Avenue, Alondra Boulevard, and Wilmington Avenue. In 2025 the city recorded 333 injury collisions and 484 people injured, with reports clustering on Fridays between 4 and 6 p.m. These are simply record counts; they reflect where traffic volume is, not a verdict about any particular street.

items.question: How long do I have to file an injury claim in California?
items.answer: For most personal injury claims, the deadline is two years from the date of the injury. If your claim is against a government entity, such as a city bus or a public road defect, you may have only six months to file a claim. Talking with an attorney early helps protect those deadlines.

items.question: What if I was partly to blame for my accident?
items.answer: California follows pure comparative fault. Your compensation is reduced by whatever share of fault is assigned to you, but you are not barred from recovering. An attorney can help sort out how fault is likely to be divided.

items.question: How much will it cost me to hire an attorney?
items.answer: Our connection service is free, and attorneys in our network work on contingency. That means no attorney fee unless there is a recovery in your case. Fee percentages and any case costs are explained by the attorney before you sign anything.
